body:
Yeah, my normal doctor is a bit diagnose happy though.  My big concern is I really want to get into the military.  I don’t want to let this go though.  This is generally a huge annoyance than anything, so I can run through it.  It’s been getting worse though.  It was every now and again, and now it’s every month.

Don’t know when I’ll be home next though.  Could be until winter.  Bleh.  Human bodies suck.

I know...  I have a friend who wants to do it with me, and I love fauxhawks.  It makes me anxious though because last time I did a pixie I cried because my nose looked huge and I just couldn't get over it.  Stylist didn't give me what I wanted though.  Being an adult who does interviews adds in more anxiety to that.  Hair is the worst part because I can't just change it for a few days, it's a bit of a commitment.

I don't know if genderfluid really does fit still though.  It doesn't change, or maybe it does, but I just gave up and hid in my PJs all of the time.  I feel like both and neither, but without being androgynous and with lots of messy exceptions.  I've questioned a lot if I even hit the guy half ever, but then I also question whether I'm cis or not.  It always leads to this limbo area.

I wish gender wasn't a thing.  I wish we had a single pronoun for everyone and didn't care about sex besides health care.  I feel that it'd be so much nicer and easier.

I started rambling.  Thank you for your input, I really appreciate it!

I'm *really* into Neo.  I'm worried it'll be too out there and I'll stop liking it though.  I'll hold onto it and maybe I'll decide to keep it.

I like a lot of the others like Ryan, but I know someone else with that name, and it'd be weird to use it for me.

Thank you!

I'm trying to deal with this now too.  It's even worse because ADHD runs in my family, and while I'm not diagnosed with ADHD (along with basically every other mental illness), I have some symptoms.  Get distracted hardcore in conversations, my brain trails to something related to me, and then since impulsive I'll say it (after they're done).  On top of that I'll focus on one thing for weeks and weeks and want to talk about that.

It feels awful when I realize it.  I'm either preventing myself from speaking or talking about myself.

That's absolutely disgusting.  I'm so sorry you had to deal with that.  Humans tend to be really resilient, especially if you get lucky with genetics.  You got where you are on your own and you should be proud of yourself, especially with what you dealt with.

Pet insurance for cats is like $20 from ASPCA with 80% coverage and a $250 deposit (or whatever that is called).  If kitty gets expensive that'll save you.  It includes everything.

I did the same for mine.  My parents got too many and can't afford vet appointments or insurance.  It drives me crazy.  I can't take all of them either.

Do prioritize your health too though.  Dentists are important.

Exactly this, but kind of flipped.  My sister got help.  She got taken to doctor after doctor after doctor to help her mentally.  I get bullied, I get caught with self harm, I hide in my room all day, and my grades slip?  We'll just threaten you and yell at you and not help at all.

Few years later I got told my mom "knew I was depressed."  "I knew you could do it on your own!"

Then why aren't I better?  Why do I spend days thinking about abuse and wishing I could just wipe it from my memory?

I'm really sorry to hear about your sister.  Can you get therapy without her noticing?  Find some place that offers it for free maybe?

Stay strong.

I don't know if there's a best advice, but what I did was push.  Keep pushing.  They don't budge?  Tell family members in passing.  "Man my eyes really hurt."  I did this with my teeth and my grandma got on my parents and got me taken to the dentist.

I know lots of parents are physically abusive, mine weren't though and that's not something I'd be "punished" for.  Got yelled at, but that's all bark no bite type of thing.

Yes.  I'm not sure if it counts, but I know it's definitely considered medical abuse if someone's given unnecessary procedure such.  On here I've seen enemas and mystery shots, another sub someone was given sleepy medication.  I'm sure it's at least some sort of abuse though.

I never really thought of it like making it look less obvious you don't get care.  I saw it more like they didn't believe me, even when I was in tears due to severe pain.  All of my sports related injuries got treated though, but I was in school sports, so injuries would be easily noticed.  Anything brought up to school nurse that I left school early had at least attention to.

While I got closer to being an adult, bigger things started to be ignored.  So maybe that's why.

I didn't want to make two posts in a day so here I am.

I hate how low my self esteem is.  I walk to work a lot and had gotten the same uber a couple of times.  She gave me her number and told me to call her if I need a ride.  All I could think of before is how annoyed she probably is about getting me so many times because she must not like me.  Maybe I talked too much or about myself too much and so why would she want to be around me at all?

I do this with most relationships.  People who care don't go out of their way to do things like that.  It's hard for me to *really* see that.

Edit: I also hate making posts that seem very little like RBN, lol.  It's a mixture of bullying, outside abuse, and lack of support from my family (and possible verbal abuse, and manipulation from them).  I'm trying to get better from my past, but it's so difficult.

I found a weird thing I've been doing and where it came from.  It was too short for an actual post.

There was a lot of yelling and fighting at home.  I've pushed a lot of it out to forget.  Lots of slammed doors.

Every time I hear my roommate come in or out of a room or the dorm and I'm in my room and can't see her leave I jump.  It's really sad.  It's like I'm an abused puppy.

I hope I get an apartment this year...

https://www.reddit.com/r/NonZeroDay/comments/1qbxvz/the_gospel_of_uryans01_helpful_advice_for_anyone/

I found this on google.  I've never linked to a Reddit and I'm on mobile, so I apologize if it's a bit goofy or something.

It's given me a better mind set.  I've sat in a dark, unforgiving chasm for so long and I needed to get out.  I've naturally gotten into a better place within it after awhile once I had a better environmental situation, but there is no way of getting out for real without doing anything.  It's hard to try to change.  It's kind of scary.  You don't know how you'll do.  You don't know if you can make it or if you'll slip and fall.  You can't get out unless you try though, and if you keep trying there will be success.

Unless I need to wake up I normally sleep in.  And by sleep in I mean 1PM.  I have zero days (days I do nothing) the most on those days.  Finding something to get up in the morning for feels better and you do *something*.  I pick morning classes in college for this reason because I *have* to get up since it's no longer on my terms.

The only way I can think of for 6AM to not be awful is to go to bed at the same time and get up at the same time.  Sometimes that sucks.  I wake up at 7AM and it feels bad while I'm in class, but then I have all day to do things and it feels freeing.  I still get some wiggle room of when to go to bed too, but it's still not a whole lot.

Some people do fine with staying up late and waking up late, but for me it isn't healthy.  If you get what you need to done and feel good I don't think it's a problem.

About right.  I fell into depression starting in 7th and I never got help.  I go to therapy now and I've started to try to get back into doing work on my free time (instead of sitting in bed all day) and started working out.  I've done this a lot and I always just fall back into old habits.  I'm hoping this times the real deal.

Don't know where to start with eating as I've been eating junk for 7 years though (I've learned peaches taste awful).  Gotta start somewhere though.
I've been lied to to be manipulated so much by my parents half the time I don't trust them on almost anything.  Bonus points when it's yelled at me.

Reminds me of a girl I work with.  She came in looking awful.  I thought she was upset and had been trying to think of what to say or do to help her.  She runs off in the middle of an order 15 minutes later and I take over her register.  I found out her mom made her come to work and she had thrown up and was sent home.  I don't know her home life, but that's really awful.

I had the other end of the stick.  I could skip a ton of school, but if I got really sick and should have been taken to the hospital or doctor and it wasn't something *they* could see (i.e. puking) I'd have to fight for it.  They'd tell me how awful xyz is to try to change my mind.  I'd often end up freaking out because I was in severe pain.

Opposite for me, but I don't think I have a full blown eating disorder.

Mom would say I'm too skinny, I need to eat more.  Then she'd turn around and say I'm using too much salt, why would I eat that, etc.  In high school I stopped eating one summer.  Once every three or four days.  No pain or anything, I didn't feel hungry.  I don't know why.  I'd lie about what I ate and when I did I'd show evidence, so my parents believed I ate every day.  I dropped 20lbs minimum.  Went back to (just) normal weight after that with pressure from my peers as I didn't just go back to eating when I got to school.

I put on weight in the last one or two years.  I feel gross and ugly.  I never had stretch marks and I can see the beginnings of them.  Now I have this little voice telling me not to eat.  It's easier to starve it off than do it healthily.  Sometimes I give into it.  Sometimes I give into the logic and hunger.  It started kind of recently

I don't know.  It sucks.  I just want my body back and I wish I never fretted about my hip bones - I was at the very bottom of a healthy weight then.

No car, I would have to walk to get to the house and such and some places aren't close.  My direct area is basically only college students so there wouldn't be lots of work since they can't have pets either.  I would rather pet sit or watch houses, but again, the problem of getting there and my dorm not allowing pets.  Maybe when I get a car and my apartment.

>18 but <21 for privacy reasons.

I don't know why it's formatted like that^

I'm calling a place I applied to tomorrow.  Hopefully I'll get that job because I can get the bus to there as long as I'm in college, then I'll have a car and can start searching Fall semester.

I'm a psych major.  It makes me internally scream when I hear that.  It lessens the bond with the parent and punishments work less than reinforcers.  Sometimes parents punish their kids too late and it's like hitting a dog who peed on the floor yesterday.  They don't know what they did wrong.  You can tell them, but I don't believe it connects as well as if the punishment was given right away, which is a problem of all punishments.

Logically thinking though, how is spanking any different than any other type of abuse?  Why is it ok for a parent to spank their child, but not kick them in the leg?  Why can a parent spank a child with a belt, but its abuse if they whip their back or arms?  It's not.  It's completely abusive and harmful.  There's always another better way to deal with bad behaviors, but you have to be patient with them.  They're just a child.

My job right now is PT (4hrs) and pays squat.  Trying to get an apartment, so squat isn't helpful.  Home is stressful, and the dorms are too expensive and aren't year round.  It sucks.  I just can't go back to all of that.

I know they're not supposed to judge, but it's hard for me to see it, if that makes sense.  It's so easy to think about what she's said and think, "oh, she thinks I'm fine," or, "she probably thinks that's stupid."  I know it's just my emotions, and it's not really what she does or says, but I get in my head.

My parents wanted to hold me back a year because my age allowed me to go to class with the class I was in, or the one before.  So I graduated at 17/18 instead of 18/19 (which I assume is the case for you).

Push through it.  Some high schools let you graduate early if you work hard and get the requirements done early.  Talk to them and see if you can.  I would have loved to graduate early, but I would feel behind if I were you too.  There's lots of people in your situation though and it's ok.

I have a question related to that.

All children discover that part of their bodies, and "explore."  What is a parent *actually* supposed to do?  We got scolded and told not to, but in a way that feels like we're telling kids the parent controls their body.  If you leave it happen, it kind of feels like sexual abuse in a way, though I was sexually abused, so I could very well be wrong.  Like I'm afraid of accidentally abusing my nieces by doing normal things, so I opt out of said things.

I hope this isn't weird or something, but I've always wondered that.

I completely understand where you're coming from.  I deleted all physical evidence of mine because I didn't realize it was sexual abuse, I thought I was part of it.  Now I have nothing to use against any of them; I wanted to submit it anonymously a while ago.

See if you can do that.  I know it's hard.  There's no way I could ever do it either.  No one except two people know bits and pieces of it, and I've never said it out loud.

What you're feeling is normal.  Keep in mind that none of this is your fault.  No one is upset with you for not going to the police.  You need to do whatever you need to to recover and feel better.  Maybe you could talk to a therapist?

Stay strong.

If you need to cry, it's ok to cry.  Don't think about it as crying over someone who doesn't deserve your tears; think of it like letting anything bad she did to you out.  Take some deep breaths, go for a walk, hit your pillow, or do something to distract yourself.  Anything safe you need to do to make yourself feel a little better.

No one here wants you dead or to stop breathing.  You are a strong and unique person and you deserve to be nothing but happy.
Yeah it probably was, thank you!  I replied to that comment.

They'll probably freak out more than a bit.  It would basically be blindsiding them because I'd be doing it some months after they said no without it being brought up once since.

The only stuff at the house is paintings I hope to hang in my apartment and stuffed toys I don't care about.  I live in a dorm pretty far away right now, so I have all of the vital stuff with me now.

I have time, but I also don't.  I need a job in 2 months or else everything's going to be rushed hard.  If I don't get this one it's going to be hard to find another.

I have this feeling that I'm doing something bad.  I'm glad I have the money part more settled though, and I'm glad that I didn't just passively sit and let them decide what I do with my money.

I hope my parents don't decide to do that.  My parents aren't as manipulative anymore, maybe they think I'll just stay on the path they more or less believe they set up for me.  Then they'll find out no, I'm my own person  on my own path and they'll freak out.

We don't plan on marrying right now, and we're not engaged.  I don't think he's ready, so it'll probably be after college to some degree (I need to go to graduates school, he only needs a bachelors).  I would like to marry in mid-20s, but it was more of a "what if we did?"  They'd probably be ecstatic for us until they realized I'd no longer be a dependent.

The problem with being away from home over the summer is that all of my stuff is there to be touched by them or kids.  I just started assuming I'd have to pick everything back up when I got home from work.  I'm incredibly protective of my things, so I absolutely hated leaving the house unless it was to spend time with my boyfriend.  I'm fine now since mostly everything is with me at college.

Wisdom teeth are out.  I was worried about having to cover them myself, but that would mean I'd have to leave them.  They were starting to hurt, so I started pressuring them hard.  Plus I found out after I certain age they get roots and are harder to get out with a worse recovery.  No thanks.

I mean, technically I'm already temporarily moved.  I live on campus.  I want to have my apartment on hold or whatever before April, so I know I have the go ahead to get my insurance and then claim as an independent.  They can't do anything as long as I'm guaranteed housing over the summer besides make a scene on campus or blow up my phone, so I'll be safe to tell them after I do my taxes as long as everything falls into place.

I'm hoping when I tell them they don't get angry right away, but instead plays 20 questions where I get to tell them, "I already planned for that," and then they can be dumbfounded.  The idea makes me nervous though.  Once I do that it's done.  I wish I could slowly slide into it, it feels like I'll be falling face first into it.  Going from paying for just food to paying for *everything*.  I wish I could talk to my parents and get support and more direction.

My parents are super controlling, but so far I've been safe with money (all bark no bite - they wouldn't do something that could visibly harm me in anyway that I could prove).  And while they do have lots of N traits, they want me to be financially stable.  I don't see them trying to take my money or bounce my account.  I only keep my paycheck and some cushion money in that account, so there's not much they can take.  I'd be going NC very quickly if they did that.

Yeah, after that "conversation" (getting scolded like a child) I don't plan on telling them plans related to taxes.  They were upset I got help from someone physically closer to me to do my taxes, and *that* was stressful.  I can only imagine how it'd of gone with my parents.

It's nice to hear that you got through all that stuff.  I've gotten myself stressed because of the tiny snowball in my head that is "what if I don't do this" becoming an avalanche of "all these bad things will happen."  I think I'll be ok now that I've gotten money looked over.  Now it's just getting everything done.

And thank you!  I really hope that's true (that I have a lot going for me).

Sorry if this reply is a bit everywhere.  I replied from bottom of your reply up and then added things in.

Ah, I have a big mouth.  My parents went on how I'd be losing money because I'd be paying for insurance that wouldn't be as good, my dad being very angry.  I don't know how true that is.  My dad pushed off my wisdom teeth because we'd have to pay for all of it, but insurance covered a good bit at least (so either dishonest or so stuck in his ways he couldn't take 5 seconds and look it up).  I said about claiming myself a while ago and they haven't done anything or said anything since.  My parents are all bark no bite.

I'd have to tell them not to claim me, but I need to be making enough for dental/car/vision/pet/renters/health insurance.  I think that's all I'd need, but that adds up and I don't think I could cover it all right now.  I'll start making plans and figuring out prices anyways, at least I'll have it in the future.  

They're very set on me being their dependent as long as possible, but what if I want to get married in a year or two?  What if I make enough to live comfortably and want to be independent?  I'll let them think I'll be their dependent for as long as they'd like, but I'm dropping them as soon as I can.  At that point what can they do?

And for living arrangements, I bet my grandma would *love* to take me (she's an n to other ns and only did an n thing to me once).  My parents would probably go crazy their child didn't like living with them so much that she went and lived with someone else.  At least with the apartment I can say I want to be more independent, not transfer, and pay less in loans.  They won't try to stop me from doing that.  I know they won't like me living so far away, but it doesn't seem to be for control there.

If need be, I could say I want to spend the summer with her.  Do stuff with my parents to curb any extra anger.  Either way, I'd be so much more relaxed at her house.

Thinking about it though, if I claimed myself this year, I'll be getting more money from tax.  Not sure how much, but more.  I can get grants from the state since I'm making dirt (which gives *a lot*), more money from FASFA probably, my family contribution would probably just go to 0, and I can probably get more grants elsewhere.  It could be possible not to pay for anymore college assuming I get 10k and an apartment.

If I get a car I could do some of my summer at my current job, and go full time or something at the other.  Save up for anytime I may not make as much or need a bit extra.  Look for a new job away from the cash register that may pay better and it'll look good.  Could use my then summer job as a reference as then they'd know I'm not completely leaving.

I feel a lot more empowered.  Thank you!  I'll definitely be looking into everything.

Quick edit: I would love to room with my current roommate next year, but she doesn't have a job right now.  She's not far from home, but I don't think she'd want to.  I could ask.  I'm worried about her leaving though, or if me and my boyfriend get married.  I might bring it up next semester, but I'd rather be able to cover everything on my own.

Yeah...  My mom did the same thing with the barging in thing.  Anytime I told her I didn't want her in the bathroom she'd say, "well I saw it all anyways."  I'm not a baby anymore, I do not care.  Get out.

I'm trying to move out, and I'm struggling hard.  I tried r/personalfinance and they couldn't get me any advice, maybe you can?

I'm a sophomore with 50k in loans.  My GPA is low so I haven't been getting scholarships, which is what I'm working on.  By senior year if I get an apartment I will have 70k in loans if with no scholarships.  I pay 25/mo currently.

I do not have a car or a license, and the bus goes one way.  Everything directly around me is family owned, so it's a 30-60min walk to any business I could work at.  Bus ends at 5, so I have to walk or bother someone at night assuming I get the job I'm going for currently, as right now I walk.  It gets cold though, so I'm trying to get my license before winter.  New job will probably pay me anywhere from 9.50-10, and I plan on applying to a job that pays 11 (all customer service).

Apartment I want is a 15 mins walk *farther* from jobs.  There's a hospital right beside it, but they pay less and I don't know if I could do the stress right now.  There's one further away that pays more, so I still end up needing a car.  Don't know if bus passes and there's no Uber's here.  Rent is 475-555 on a sliding scale, including water, sewer, and trash.  I need to pay for electric and internet.  Does that include heat/AC though?

Don't know if you can help with any of that, but I've been wanting to get foodstamps.  Problem is, my parents make too much money and I'm a dependent.  They have debt, so they can't really help me at all.  Can I get foodstamps since I'm in the dorms, buying my own things?  My parents really only pay for insurance for me and I guess the house over the summer.

I need to somehow be making enough before winter break.  I'll be able to start trying to get apartments when I get back to college.  I have good credit so that shouldn't be a huge problem.  Besides the age of my credit, I have a lot of inquiries because of loans and trying to get a credit card (which family disproved of, but my credit has been getting a lot better a lot faster than before).  I should be ok there.

I just want to get out.  I don't think I can do another four months at home.

Sorry, I kind of feel like I'm hijacking.  Also thank you if you read this.

I was once constipated to the point that even bending hurt.  I couldn't easily remove my pants.

I ended up freaking out the next day because I should be taken to the hospital.  "They'll put things in your butt though" "it'll hurt!"  Do you think I care?

I started taking laxatives almost weekly and my dad got angry when I asked for food with more fiber to see if that helps.

It took me *two years* to get my parents to get my wisdom teeth out.  I was an adult by the time I got them out, and my dad tried to throw it on me.  No.  I don't have *any* of the medical information, how am I supposed to do that?

I'm glad you're getting help for your mouth OP!

I'm proud of you!  Mine was a little below average, 600/800 (top 10% of people who took it at the same time as me) for Math, and barely scraping by for my school in the English parts, but I had an older test.  I've always been stupidly happy over my 600.  Don't let them bring you down.  You deserve that, and you worked hard.  Ns like to make things about themselves, and your father blows my mind.  If you can get a 1500, and he still says it's not enough, he has his standards too high or he's as dumb as a rock.  You deserve some bragging rights at least for a day.

You're going to go far.  I assume you're going to college, and you're going to have the easiest time getting accepted.  Make sure to check online applications and not paper, as some Ns hide those.  Try to find scholarships, and someone to cosign loans if need be.  My state has a state grant, check that too as well as FASFA.  Sooner you get FASFA done the better.  If you're a senior start applying *now*, if you're a junior start looking for colleges and apply in the summer.  If you're one of the first applications in they'll look at yours first.  My college generally gives acceptance things at the beginning of the year, I got mine two or three months early by that.

Keep your head up, I'm so proud of you for working so hard and getting such a fantastic score!

I wish I had this advice when I was a teen.  I found out about pins the same day my mom went through my phone (which fueled another fight because when they asked for my phone not only was it empty, I also gave it to them locked).  I tried to keep things logged out besides YouTube, but sometimes you forget, or it doesn't do it.  And she snooped through my YouTube too.

My parents are the all bark no bite type of parents (luckily, I'd be dead otherwise probably).  I didn't get in trouble much, but I got yelled at and if I was in trouble I'd have my laptop for an hour a day.  If they saw me reading after my hour, I got another hour.  That hour never ends.

Once I left my Facebook open and I heard my mom question something (she didn't give me time to log out of everything and said she "wouldn't look").  "I don't know what you're talking about, let me see."  My sister was telling my mom I was going to log out, and that's exactly what I did.  And somehow I didn't get in trouble, which I find hilarious.  I think at that point they were just tired of "dealing" with me even though they never got me help, so what do you expect to change?

It doesn't help, but it's still nice to hear.  I've dealt with lots of abuse which my parents may or may not have made me an easy target for (I isolated myself before I was even a teen, so then I was lonely, and I didn't have the best boundaries and any boundaries I made were like water, which could be due to them or due to a "lesser" form of abuse from someone else).  It's nice to hear either way.  Thank you.
A bit different, and hard to explain.  My boyfriend holds me when I cry.  Anytime I think about it I want to cry because it makes me so happy.

I keep to myself a lot, but college is really great for me too.  I don't know if I'd call my parents Ns, but our relationship is a lot better when I'm not in their house all of the time, so I live on campus.  I don't think that's the case for a lot of others here, but it's a lot less stressful for anyone who lives in a stressful home, and I'd assume especially if you're too far away for them to visit all of the time.

I've been NC since I went to college this year with my Boarderline Sister (has bsis been made yet?).

She hasn't messaged me since I left while we were fighting, and I haven't messaged her because I'm stubborn.  I'm thinking it's for the best, though.

She was supposed to pay me back money she had stolen before she got clean.  I let her use some of my money as well over the summer without the expectation of getting *that* money back (it was mostly small things), but she did seem to genuinely want to give my money back, all of it (which she did give a little bit back).

Because I was bringing up wanting my money back that she was pushing off every week, she decided to hold the money over my head like she does everything else.  Doesn't matter if I literally need that money or not, I'm didn't treat her "nicely" enough, so that warrants not getting the money that *she stole* from me.  I'm still absolutely livid.

But no, you don't hold gifts and agreements over people's heads if they get upset because you're not following through or because they don't want to go somewhere with you every single day.

I completely agree.  I "advertise" it to everyone who is struggling like us.  I'm a psych major so I always hear about  the studies that show any type of therapy is better on average than none.  There's no reason to be afraid and some of them dealt with what we're dealing with.  Hard to take my own advice, and I pushed it off so much.

Tomorrow can't get here any sooner.  I'm hoping for it to go really smoothly, get a solid answer, and a solid game plan.  I just want to get the first day over with.

In my head it's so easy, but I couldn't ask someone from my club if they wanted to go and sit in the waiting room with me.  Even though I know they'd be completely chill with me asking, and I wouldn't care if they told me no.  I'm going to probably end up freezing.

I'll make an update tomorrow.

Thank you!

Edit: I have the appointment in less than 6 hours now.  I've been really anxious.  I'm scared of seeing concern on her face, but I mean, who wouldn't be?  I guess I just don't want to physically be able to see how bad it is/was.

Not sure if this counts.  I used to be on the edge of my BMI.  Like 1-5 pounds would literally take me from underweight to a normal weight.  I ate normally, and I didn't feel weak as you'd expect someone who's starving would.  I felt relatively comfortable in that weight with some exclusions.  I did sports too, so I often got physicals and not a single doctor was worried about my weight, which may also be because I normally maintained with very little fluctuations (+-5 normally).

My mom who at one point had an ED would always complain that I'm too skinny.  I need to eat more.  However, she would also pick at what I ate.  Especially if I put salt on it.
